name: Desovane
description: The pharmacological inverse of sensitizers like Velastrin, Desovane is a licensed SNT-interface suppressor that reduces or eliminates feedback from augmented systems. Medically used for pain management in patients with damaged chrome interfaces, for high-stress surgical augment procedures, and for managing hypersensitivity disorders. Its street use is more troubling: people take it to not feel their augments — for dissociation, for numbness, or to commit violence without the physical feedback of what their chrome is doing.
effects: Tactile and proprioceptive feedback from augments reduced 80-100%
Pain from damaged or malfunctioning chrome eliminated
Psychological detachment from augmented body parts
Augments continue to function normally — user simply cannot feel them
Useful for operating through augment damage that would otherwise be incapacitating
side_effects: Inability to detect augment malfunction or damage during effect
Psychological dissociation extending beyond chrome to organic body
Rare: users lose track of augmented limb positions, causing accidental injury to self or others
Long-term use associated with permanent reduction in augment sensitivity
cultural_context: Desovane has a dark reputation that its clinical applications don't deserve. Medically, it's essential — patients with chrome nerve damage would be in constant agony without it. On the street, it's used by people who want to be numb: trauma survivors who hate their augments, fixers who need to do violence without feeling it, and a disturbing subculture of Shelf residents who dissociate entirely from their chrome as a coping mechanism for the horror of their daily lives. Lazarus lobbies hard to keep it prescription-only but the street supply is substantial.
story_hooks: A series of violent incidents in Tier 2 are linked by a detail: the perpetrators all tested positive for Desovane, all claim they 'didn't feel' what they were doing. Someone may be distributing the drug specifically to create deniable violence.

A Tier 3 augment surgeon is quietly supplying Desovane to Shelf patients who can't afford legitimate pain management for their failing chrome — the practice is illegal but the need is real, and someone wants it stopped

A contact goes quiet — when found, they're on a continuous Desovane patch cycle, completely dissociated from their heavily augmented body. Someone did this to them deliberately, and the question is why they needed this person unable to feel
